beats.text: Bad sleep makes couples fight more. That's science!
Berkeley psychologists asked people in relationships to track their sleep and their fights for two weeks.
After a bad night, they had more conflict the next day. Even good sleepers! And in the lab?
Tired couples were worse at reading each other's feelings!
So before the big talk: sleep on it. Literally!

ask: SEND THIS TO YOUR TIRED PARTNER.
sources: Gordon & Chen (2014), The role of sleep in interpersonal conflict: Do sleepless nights mean worse fights?, Social Psychological and Personality Science 5(2) – Study 1: 78 people in relationships, 14-day diary: more conflict after poor sleep; Study 2: 71 couples in the lab: after poor sleep, more negative affect during conflict and lower empathic accuracy.
